Based on what you've said above and as a response, it sounds a lot like you have one of those thrice-damned bluetooth/wifi combo cards that Dell likes to put into some models. If that's the case, even though you've said you don't have a "proper switch," it's very likely that the device is set to "bluetooth only" mode. There will be an fn-function key combo you can use to cycle the card through its various modes, and depending on what model laptop you have, you might even get status lights telling you what's being turned on and off, but failing that, you'll need to tail -f /var/log/messages or demsg | tail to see if the system is recognizing any new devices.

If you can't get anywhere with that, then do an lspci -vnn | grep Net to see what network devices your system can see. The -vnn will give us verbose output and list the PCI vendor and device codes, allowing us to identify precisely what driver is required for your hardware.

Totalbiscuit: I will now talk about Oculus Rift for 27 minutes
Spot on. (I don't totally agree with his monitor comparison and optics comments but it's a reasonable view)

Yeah, if you're upset that it's $600 because Oculus' message has suggested a much lower price point, then I understand your frustration.

However, if you're complaining because "you also have to spend $350 on a 970 which increases the cost" then this device isn't meant for you. This was obviously an enthusiast level device from the start. Remember, their recommended specs (which is the 970 and an i5-4590) are just to get games running properly. It's not for people who say 'If it was $300, then I'd spend $350 on a 970'. It's for people who already have a titan or a 980 and were thinking about buying a 2nd one. Or someone with a beefy rig thinking of getting a new 4K display.

Speaking of which. If you can comfortably wear an Oculus for several hours, then compared to a monitor with similar specs it's actually comparatively inexpensive. Since the device is on your face, then a giant screen would be the only comparison, and I don't know of any 50" + screens that have this resolution, refresh rate, and latency, anywhere near this price point.

Does this suck? Yes. Is this surprising? Only if you took Palmer Lucky's 'ballpark $350" quote as gospel.

I'm interested to see what the compatibility is going to be. If you can get a large enough selection of games/applications then it would be worth it for the experience. The price is about the same in the UK for a 4k TV.

However if the selection is limited, artificially or because of technology, then I can't see it catching on. In the UK a 4k TV is not worth it because there is hardly anything to actually watch.

I'll be waiting until next year.
